'''Eusébio da Silva Ferreira''' ({{IPA|pt-PT|ewˈzɛβju ðɐ ˈsilvɐ fɨˈʁɐjɾɐ|lang}}; 25 January 1942 – 5 January 2014), nicknamed the "'''Black Panther'''",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid=2496768/ |title=Gone but not forgotten |date=31 December 2014 |website=fifa.com |publisher=[[FIFA]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103014253/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid%3D2496768/ |archive-date= 3 January 2015 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2016 }}</ref> the "'''Black Pearl'''"<ref name="worldcup">{{Cite news |date=6 June 2010 |title=From Africa to posterity: How Eusébio lit up the World Cup |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jun/06/eusebio-africa-world-cup |access-date=7 June 2013 |archive-date=24 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324065401/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jun/06/eusebio-africa-world-cup |url-status=live }}</ref> or "'''o Rei'''" ("the King"),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnoticias.pt/etiqueta/eusebio|title=Eusébio|publisher=dnoticias.Pt|access-date=11 January 2014|quote=Segundo António Vitalino Dantas, "Eusébio foi realmente o primeiro e maior futebolista da África e de Portugal" e um "grande embaixador" de Moçambique e de Portugal e é considerado "o rei" do futebol." [According to António Vitalino Dantas, "Eusébio was actually the first and greatest footballer of Africa and Portugal" and a "great ambassador" for Mozambique and Portugal and is considered "the king" of football."]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140111014616/http://www.dnoticias.pt/etiqueta/eusebio|archive-date=11 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.noticias-do-futebol.com/content/eus%C3%A9bio-destaca-n%C3%ADvel-de-cr7|title=Eusébio destaca nível de CR7|publisher=noticias-do-futebol.com|access-date=11 January 2014|quote=Hoje e sempre o Rei do futebol português, Eusébio ... [Now and always the king of Portuguese football, Eusébio ...]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111032201/http://www.noticias-do-futebol.com/content/eus%C3%A9bio-destaca-n%C3%ADvel-de-cr7|archive-date=11 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> was a Portuguese [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]]. He is considered one of the greatest players of all time<ref name="Stokkermans">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/iffhs-century.html |title=IFFHS' Century Elections |first=Karel |last=Stokkermans |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |date=30 January 2000 |access-date=10 March 2009 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303065744/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/iffhs-century.html |archive-date=3 March 2009 }}</ref><ref name="BBC-Obit">{{cite web |url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25611509 |title = Eusebio: Portugal football legend dies aged 71 |publisher = BBC Sport |date = 5 January 2014 |access-date = 5 January 2014 |archive-date = 12 June 2015 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150612095758/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/25611509 |url-status = live }}</ref> as well as [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]'s best player ever.<ref name="poligrafo">{{Cite web|url=https://poligrafo.sapo.pt/fact-check/eusebio-vinha-para-o-sporting-mas-foi-desviado-pelo-benfica-no-aeroporto-de-lisboa|title=Eusébio vinha para o Sporting mas foi "desviado" pelo Benfica no aeroporto de Lisboa? (Com vídeo)|access-date=24 May 2021|archive-date=24 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524004523/https://poligrafo.sapo.pt/fact-check/eusebio-vinha-para-o-sporting-mas-foi-desviado-pelo-benfica-no-aeroporto-de-lisboa|url-status=live}}</ref> He was known for his speed, technique, athleticism and right-footed shot, making him a prolific goalscorer, accumulating 733 goals in 745 matches.<ref name="BBC-Obit" /> Eusébio was the first ever player to win [[European Golden Shoe|European Golden Boot]], [[World Cup Golden Boot]] and [[List of UEFA Champions League top scorers|UCL Golden Boot]]. In the [[UEFA Champions League]], he ranks second for the all-time Portuguese top goalscorers, scoring 47 goals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=The official website for European football |url=https://www.uefa.com/errors/ |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref>

Eusébio helped [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] reach third place at the [[1966 FIFA World Cup]], being the [[World Cup Golden Boot|top goalscorer of the tournament]] with nine goals.<ref name="Portugal's beloved and brilliant Black Panther">{{cite web|url= https://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=39547/profile.html|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151009162729/http://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=39547/profile.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= 9 October 2015|title=Portugal's beloved and brilliant Black Panther|work=FIFA.com|access-date=20 October 2015 }}</ref> He won the [[Ballon d'Or]] in [[1965 Ballon d'Or|1965]] and was runner-up in [[1962 Ballon d'Or|1962]] and [[1966 Ballon d'Or|1966]]. He is Benfica's all-time top scorer with 473 goals in 440 competitive matches. There, his honours include eleven [[Primeira Liga]] titles and a [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], also being integral in reaching additional European Cup finals in [[1963 European Cup Final|1963]], [[1965 European Cup Final|1965]] and [[1968 European Cup Final|1968]]. He is the [[List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League top scorers#All-time top scorers|second-highest goalscorer]], behind [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], in the pre-Champions League era of the European Cup with 47 goals. He was the [[List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League top scorers#European Cup and UEFA Champions League Top Goalscorer by seasons|European Cup top scorer]] in [[1964–65 European Cup|1964–65]], [[1965–66 European Cup|1965–66]] and [[1967–68 European Cup|1967–68]]. He also won the [[Bola de Prata (Portugal)|Bola de Prata]] for the Primeira Liga top scorer a record seven times. He was the first ever player to win the [[European Golden Shoe|European Golden Boot]], in 1968, a feat he replicated in 1973.

From his retirement until his death, Eusébio was an ambassador of football and was one of the most recognizable faces of his generation. His name often appears in best player of all time lists and polls by football critics and fans. He was elected [[FIFA Player of the Century|the ninth-best footballer of the 20th century]] in a poll by the [[IFFHS]] and [[World Soccer (magazine)|the tenth-best footballer of the 20th century]] in a poll by the [[World Soccer Magazine|World Soccer]] magazine.<ref name="Stokkermans"/> [[Pelé]] named Eusébio as one of the 125 best living footballers in his 2004 [[FIFA 100]] list. He was seventh in the online poll for [[UEFA Golden Jubilee Poll]]. In November 2003, to celebrate UEFA's Jubilee, he was selected as the [[UEFA Jubilee Awards|Golden Player]] of Portugal by the [[Portuguese Football Federation]] as their most outstanding player of the past 50 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/Kind=256/newsId=130150.html |title=Golden Players take centre stage |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040312203128/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/Kind%3D256/newsId%3D130150.html |archive-date=12 March 2004 |work=[[UEFA]] |date=29 November 2003 |access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> Shortly after Eusébio's death, Di Stéfano stated: "For me Eusébio will always be the best player of all time".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/01/05/futbol/futbol_internacional/1388915262.html|title=Eusebio, 'La Pantera de Mozambique'|website=MARCA|access-date=14 February 2021|archive-date=24 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324065404/https://www.marca.com/2014/01/05/futbol/futbol_internacional/1388915262.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Eusébio was born in the Mafalala neighbourhood of [[Maputo|Lourenço Marques]] (now Maputo), [[Portuguese Mozambique]] on 25 January 1942. His parents were Laurindo António da Silva Ferreira, a white railroad worker from [[Malanje]], [[Portuguese Angola]], and his wife Elisa Anissabeni, a black Mozambican woman.<ref>[https://portuguese-american-journal.com/eusebio-portugal-and-mozambique-mourn-their-soccer-legend/ Eusébio: Portugal and Mozambique mourn their soccer legend] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901120310/https://portuguese-american-journal.com/eusebio-portugal-and-mozambique-mourn-their-soccer-legend/ |date=1 September 2019 }} Portuguese American Journal</ref> He was the fourth child of his parents out of five children (Jaime, Alberto, Adelino, Eusébio and Lucília). Elisa Anissabeni later had another three children from a second marriage (Gilberto, Inocência and Fernando).<ref name=":62">{{Cite web |last=Vaza |first=Marco |date=5 January 2014 |title=Eusébio nunca será suplente na equipa dos melhores de sempre |url=https://www.publico.pt/2014/01/05/desporto/noticia/eusebio-nunca-sera-suplente-na-equipa-dos-melhores-de-sempre-1618455 |access-date=20 November 2023 |website=PÚBLICO |language=pt}}</ref> Growing up in an extremely poor neighbourhood, he used to skip school classes to play barefoot football with his friends  (one of them was as José Manuel Alves Holbeche Bastos, whose father José Rodrigues Holbeche Bastos played professional football for Sporting Clube de Lourenço Marques) on improvised pitches and using stuffed socks as footballs. His father also played football in his youth and supported Lisbon's [[S.L. Benfica|SL Benfica]] and its affiliate team in Portuguese Mozambique, [[GD Maputo|Grupo Desportivo de Lourenço Marques]]. He died from [[tetanus]] when Eusébio was eight years old in 1950, so the widowed Elisa almost exclusively raised young Eusébio alone.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Eusébio: As lendas não morrem |url=https://www.flash.pt/celebridades/nacional/detalhe/eusebio-as-lendas-nao-morrem |access-date=9 October 2023 |website=www.flash.pt |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220229/https://www.flash.pt/celebridades/nacional/detalhe/eusebio-as-lendas-nao-morrem |url-status=live }}</ref> Absorbed by football from an early age, Eusébio studied until the 4th grade (concluded through a final exam when he was already in mainland Portugal),<ref>{{Cite web |title=A guerra para garantir Eusébio... ou Ruth com th |url=https://expresso.pt/arquivo/desporto/a-guerra-para-garantir-eusebio-ou-ruth-com-th=f848972 |access-date=12 October 2023 |website=Jornal Expresso |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220227/https://expresso.pt/arquivo/desporto/a-guerra-para-garantir-eusebio-ou-ruth-com-th=f848972 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eusébio: As lendas não morrem |url=https://www.flash.pt/celebridades/nacional/detalhe/eusebio-as-lendas-nao-morrem |access-date=12 October 2023 |website=www.flash.pt |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220229/https://www.flash.pt/celebridades/nacional/detalhe/eusebio-as-lendas-nao-morrem |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Uma longa viagem da Mafalala ao céu |url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/benfica/detalhe/uma-longa-viagem-da-mafalala-ao-ceu-861305 |access-date=17 November 2023 |website=www.record.pt |language=pt-PT}}</ref> the only among his brothers and sisters without post-[[primary education]]. Three of his siblings became engineers.<ref>"Eusébio – A minha História", João Malheiro, 2005, QN-Edição e Conteúdos, pág. 14</ref><ref name="tribuna.expresso.pt">{{Cite web |title=Eusébio: "O Sporting de Lourenço de Marques era um clube de elite, um clube da polícia, que não gostava das pessoas de cor" |url=https://tribuna.expresso.pt/arquivos-expresso/2017-01-25-Eusebio-O-Sporting-de-Lourenco-de-Marques-era-um-clube-de-elite-um-clube-da-policia-que-nao-gostava-das-pessoas-de-cor-2 |access-date=9 October 2023 |website=Tribuna Expresso |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220228/https://tribuna.expresso.pt/arquivos-expresso/2017-01-25-Eusebio-O-Sporting-de-Lourenco-de-Marques-era-um-clube-de-elite-um-clube-da-policia-que-nao-gostava-das-pessoas-de-cor-2 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Club career==

===Early career===
Eusébio first started to play for a local amateur team that he and his friends formed called ''Os Brasileiros'' (The Brazilians), in honour of the great [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]] of the 1950s. They would play under the names of some of those superstars. The balls they used were made of socks stuffed with newspapers rolled into spheres.

=== Sporting Lourenço Marques ===
With some friends, Eusébio tried to join Desportivo de Lourenço de Marques, his favourite team and a [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] [[Farm team|feeder team]] (also the team where [[Mário Coluna]] had played before his move to Benfica) but was rejected, without even being given a chance to prove his worth.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abola.pt/publica/100f/index.asp?n=f29 |title=100 figuras do futebol português |access-date=14 April 2017 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071212015215/http://www.abola.pt/publica/100f/index.asp?n=f29 |archive-date=12 December 2007 }} Retrieved 27 January 2011 (Portuguese)</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.academia-de-talentos.com/entrevista/2010/8/3/entrevista-com-nuno-martins-parte-1 |title=Entrevista com Nuno Martins (Parte 1) |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525130446/http://www.academia-de-talentos.com/entrevista/2010/8/3/entrevista-com-nuno-martins-parte-1 |archive-date=25 May 2011 |access-date=9 February 2011 |language=pt |work=[[Academia de Talentos]]|date=January 2000 }}</ref> He was also rejected by [[Clube Ferroviário de Maputo|Ferroviário de Lourenço Marques]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vaza |first=Marco |date=5 January 2014 |title=Cronologia de uma vida |url=https://www.publico.pt/2014/01/05/desporto/noticia/cronologia-de-uma-vida-1618523 |access-date=11 October 2023 |website=PÚBLICO |language=pt |archive-date=28 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928213146/https://www.publico.pt/2014/01/05/desporto/noticia/cronologia-de-uma-vida-1618523 |url-status=live }}</ref> At 12, he then tried his luck with [[Clube de Desportos do Maxaquene|Sporting Clube de Lourenço Marques]] (branch number 6 of [[Sporting Lisbon]]), which accepted him as well as a group of his friends who lived in Eusébio's neighbourhood.<ref name="tribuna.expresso.pt"/><ref name=":62" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramos |first=Carlos |date=2014-01-11 |title=Eusébio: 'Se não fosse futebolista, teria sido o melhor bailarino do mundo' |url=https://sol.sapo.pt/2014/01/11/eusebio-se-nao-fosse-futebolista-teria-sido-o-melhor-bailarino-do-mundo/ |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=Jornal SOL |language=pt-PT}}</ref> There he had his first training sessions supervised by a coaching staff, received his first ever football equipment and played competitive football in an organized way at both youth level and the main senior team.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Antigo jogador desmente Eusébio |url=https://expresso.pt/actualidade/antigo-jogador-desmente-eusebio=f691384 |access-date=8 November 2023 |website=Jornal Expresso |language=pt}}</ref> At 15, according to him, he was spotted by a former [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] goalkeeper turned scout: "When I was 15, Juventus of Italy, wanted to hire me, because one of their scouts, who had been a famous Italian goalkeeper for them, saw me and told them that there was a boy with a potential, that it would be good to take advantage while I was still unknown. Juventus proposed but my mum never wanted to hear anything from anyone". Eusébio played his first two seasons with Sporting Lourenço Marques' youth team while he also made a few appearances in the senior team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.maxaquene.co.mz/article.php3?id_article=18 |title=Memórias do Maxaquene |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110523212722/http://www.maxaquene.co.mz/article.php3?id_article=18 |archive-date=23 May 2011 |access-date=27 January 2011 |language=pt |date=17 July 2006 |work=[[Maxaquene]]}}</ref> Then he was promoted to the main squad and won the [[Moçambola|Campeonato Provincial de Moçambique]] and the Campeonato Distrital de Lourenço Marques in his last season with the club, in 1960.<ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=5 May 2020 |title=Carlos Vieira, antigo vice-presidente do Sporting, defende espaço para Eusébio no museu leonino |url=https://sol.sapo.pt/2020/05/05/carlos-vieira-antigo-vice-presidente-do-sporting-defende-espaco-para-eusebio-no-museu-leonino/ |access-date=11 October 2023 |website=Jornal SOL |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220310/https://sol.sapo.pt/2020/05/05/carlos-vieira-antigo-vice-presidente-do-sporting-defende-espaco-para-eusebio-no-museu-leonino/ |url-status=live }}</ref> From 1957 to 1960, Eusébio scored 77 goals in 42 appearances for the main team of Sporting Lourenço Marques.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

===Benfica===

====The transfer====
On 15 December 1960,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anos 60: Chega Eusébio chega o futebol |url=https://www.record.pt/exclusivos-record/cinquentenario/detalhe/anos-60-chega-eusebio-chega-o-futebol |access-date=15 November 2023 |website=www.record.pt |language=pt}}</ref> Eusébio arrived in [[Lisbon]], when he was 18 years old. However, he only joined Benfica in May 1961, as a 19-year-old, after the [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] from his local club Sporting Lourenço Marques for 400,000 [[Portuguese escudo]]s (equivalent to €193,219 in 2023)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Simulador |url=https://www.pordata.pt/simulador-inflacao-quanto-vale-hoje-o-dinheiro-do-passado |access-date=18 November 2023 |website=www.pordata.pt}}</ref> was finally unlocked. It was a lengthy process and the legality of the signing was disputed by Sporting CP, who also tried to sign him.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Na cadeira do barbeiro: as melhores histórias de Pedroto e Eusébio |url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/classico/barbeiros/na-cadeira-do-barbeiro-as-melhores-historias-de-pedroto-e-eusebio |access-date=17 November 2023 |website=Maisfutebol |language=pt}}</ref> In the first few weeks of 1961, the Portuguese Directorate-General for Sports ruled in favour of Sporting CP's interests; soon after, the [[Portuguese Football Federation]] ruled in favour of Benfica's arguments.<ref name=":2" /> The agreement to sign Eusébio with Benfica's local representative (Rodrigues de Carvalho, a [[Major (rank)|major]])<ref name=":5" /> had been mediated in Mozambique, in June 1960,<ref name=":5" /> by one of Eusébio's brothers who was an engineer by training and intervened as an informal [[sports agent]] on behalf of his brother, and included the payment of 250,000 Portuguese escudos to Elisa Anissabene, Eusébio's mother (an initial offer of 110,000 escudos which raised to the final 250,000 escudos in November<ref name=":5" /> amid growing interest from other football clubs).<ref>{{Cite web |last=SAPO |title=Eusébio vinha para o Sporting mas foi "desviado" pelo Benfica no aeroporto de Lisboa? |url=https://poligrafo.sapo.pt/fact-check/eusebio-vinha-para-o-sporting-mas-foi-desviado-pelo-benfica-no-aeroporto-de-lisboa |access-date=14 October 2023 |website=Polígrafo |language=pt |archive-date=24 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524004523/https://poligrafo.sapo.pt/fact-check/eusebio-vinha-para-o-sporting-mas-foi-desviado-pelo-benfica-no-aeroporto-de-lisboa |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Eusébio: "O Sporting de Lourenço de Marques era um clube de elite, um clube da polícia, que não gostava das pessoas de cor" |url=https://tribuna.expresso.pt/arquivos-expresso/2017-01-25-Eusebio-O-Sporting-de-Lourenco-de-Marques-era-um-clube-de-elite-um-clube-da-policia-que-nao-gostava-das-pessoas-de-cor |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=Tribuna Expresso |language=pt}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=15 December 2010 |title=Há 50 anos o futebol português mudou |url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/benfica/ha-50-anos-o-futebol-portugues-mudou-1735146.html |access-date=17 November 2023 |website=www.dn.pt |language=pt-PT}}</ref> Benfica discovered Eusébio through the efforts of Brazilian former player [[José Carlos Bauer]], who saw him at Lourenço Marques in 1960.<ref name="tribuna.expresso.pt"/> Although he preferred playing with his right foot, Eusébio could use his left just as well. At times, Eusébio would surprise opponents with his dribbling ability, seemingly a talent he preferred to keep secret. Bauer first recommended Eusébio to his former club, [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]], but they turned him down.

Bauer had been asked by his former coach at São Paulo, [[Béla Guttmann]], to keep an eye out for talented players during a ten-week tour to Africa, and when São Paulo could not afford the asking price for Eusébio, Bauer then recommended him to Guttmann, who was coaching Benfica at the time.<ref name = "placar especial">"Os vice-campeões", Max Gehringer, ''Especial Placar: A Saga da Jules Rimet'' fascículo 4 – 1950 Brasil, dezembro de 2005, Editora Abril, págs. 46–47</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Inverting the pyramid: the history of soccer tactics|author=Wilson, Jonathan|isbn=9781568589190|edition= Second trade paperback |location=New York, NY|oclc=1024085926|date = 14 August 2018}}</ref> Guttman moved quickly and signed him.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://h2g2.com/edited_entry/A2027017 |title=h2g2 – Eusebio – A Footballing Legend |publisher=BBC |date=25 January 1942 |access-date=27 January 2011 |archive-date=29 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629062258/http://www.bbc.co.uk/dna/h2g2/A2027017 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Eusebio (1963 version2).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Eusébio during his time at Benfica. He is the [[S.L. Benfica#Individual|club's record goalscorer]], with 473 goals in 440 competitive matches.]]

Sporting Lourenço Marques was an affiliate team of Sporting CP, and the Portuguese club disputed the legality of his transfer to Benfica.<ref>{{Cite web |last=SAPO |title=Cromos da História dos Mundiais: Eusébio, a 'Pantera Negra' que conquistou a Inglaterra e fez sonhar Portugal em 1966 |url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/mundial/artigos/cromos-da-historia-dos-mundiais-eusebio-da-silva-ferreira-a-pantera-negra-que-conquistou-a-inglaterra-e-fez-sonhar-portugal-em-1966 |access-date=11 October 2023 |website=SAPO Desporto |language=pt |archive-date=30 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130161937/https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/mundial/artigos/cromos-da-historia-dos-mundiais-eusebio-da-silva-ferreira-a-pantera-negra-que-conquistou-a-inglaterra-e-fez-sonhar-portugal-em-1966 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title="Magagaga era o gajo que trepava", conta Hilário sobre Eusébio |url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/noticias/magagaga-era-o-gajo-que-trepava-conta-hilario-sobre-eusebio-5721541.html/ |access-date=15 November 2023 |website=O Jogo |language=pt}}</ref> Eusébio once said: "I used to play for Sporting's feeder club in Mozambique. Benfica wanted to pay me in a contract to go [to Portugal] while Sporting wanted to take me as a junior player for the experience with no monetary reward. Benfica made a nice approach. They went to speak to my mum, my brother, and offered €1,000 for three years. My brother asked for double and they paid it. They signed the contract with my mother and she got the money. [...] Sporting tried to spread the story that I'd stitched them up, but it was the other way round, because they tried to take me for free while Benfica were willing to pay."<ref name=worldcup/>

[[Hilário (footballer, born 1939)|Hilário]], a friend of Eusébio since childhood and former colleague at the Mozambican club, tried to convince Eusébio to go to Sporting CP. Hilário went to Benfica's dorms, met Eusébio there and Eusébio left the building with Hilário. On behalf of Sporting CP, Hilário offered him an improved professional contract instead of a [[Trial (association football)|trial period]] at the club. Sporting CP's contract offer was double Benfica's, included the necessary funds to allow financial compensation to Benfica for the incurred costs to date, and, according to Hilário, he was successful in that endeavor, but at the end of the day he left Eusébio to rest overnight back in the dorms.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hilário e Eusébio: "Foi um desgosto não ter vindo para o Sporting" |url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/liga/benfica/hilario-e-eusebio-foi-um-desgosto-nao-ter-vindo-para-o-sporting |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=Maisfutebol |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hilário: Eusébio fugiu para assinar pelo Sporting |url=https://expresso.pt/arquivo/desporto/hilario-eusebio-fugiu-para-assinar-pelo-sporting=f689566 |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=Jornal Expresso |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title="Eusébio não foi tratado no Sporting com racismo" |url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/sporting/detalhe/eusebio-nao-foi-tratado-no-sporting-com-racismo-727916 |access-date=15 November 2023 |website=www.record.pt |language=pt}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> Benfica found this meeting suspicious and instructed Eusébio to be codenamed '''Ruth Malosso'''.<ref name="goaldentimes">{{cite web|title=The Legend of Ruth Malosso : "This being a highly sensitive issue, the Benfica board decided that they will never use Eusébio's name in any communication before the deal finalizes, and thus given a code name – Ruth Malosso"|url=http://www.goaldentimes.org/the-legend-of-ruth-malosso/|website=Goalden Times|access-date=11 February 2015|date=5 January 2014|archive-date=16 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716083627/http://www.goaldentimes.org/the-legend-of-ruth-malosso/|url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, fearing a "kidnapping" attempt by Sporting CP, Benfica moved Eusébio on 8 April 1961 to a holiday home owned by Domingos Claudino, former president of Benfica, and a hotel near the Meia Praia beach, in [[Lagos, Portugal|Lagos]], [[Algarve]] region, where he would remain for twelve days until the transfer upheaval calmed down (Eusébio was awarded his 4th grade diploma while he was hidden in the Algarve).<ref name=":2" /> Fearing that Eusébio would "escape", Benfica's representatives reportedly warned him of the "danger of being run over". Eusébio then told his mother: "Mum, I'm going back because there are men here who want to hurt me."<ref name=":4" /> In the early hours of 13 May 1961, those in charge of Eusébio's transfer to Benfica occasionally bumped into Jaime Catarino Duarte, son of António Catarino Duarte who was the president of the club at the time,<ref name=":3" /> and the son of the president wanted to know where the case stood. He was told that almost everything had been taken care of, with just 400,000 escudos (400 ''[[conto]]s'') missing before Eusébio could finally be registered by Benfica. Catarino Duarte provided the necessary funds and the transfer was finalized.<ref name=":2" />

====Debut and career====
The transferring of Eusébio's registration from Sporting Lourenço Marques to Benfica was concluded and he made his first appearance for them against [[Atlético Clube de Portugal]] in a [[Exhibition game|friendly game]] on 23 May 1961. He scored a [[hat-trick]] in a 4–2 victory.<ref>[http://www.lpfp.pt/futebol/Pages/GrandesFiguras.aspx As Grandes Figuras do Futebol Português] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100328091814/http://www.lpfp.pt/futebol/Pages/GrandesFiguras.aspx |date=28 March 2010 }} Retrieved 26 January 2011. (Portuguese)</ref> His debut in an official match was on 1 June 1961, against [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]], in the third round second leg of the 1960–61 [[Taça de Portugal]]. The game was controversially scheduled for the day after the [[1961 European Cup Final|European Cup final]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and the [[Portuguese Football Federation]] did not postpone it. As the first team was returning from [[Bern]], Benfica played with the reserve squad and was defeated 1–4. Eusébio scored a goal and missed a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] (the first of only five he missed throughout his career), but this was not enough to win the round (4–5 on aggregate). On 10 June 1961, Eusébio played for the first time in the [[Primeira Liga|Primeira Divisão]], the last match day against [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]], where he scored a goal in a 4–0 win. On 15 June, Benfica played the final of the invitational [[Tournament of Paris|Tournoi de Paris]] against [[Pelé]]'s [[Santos FC|Santos]], and in the beginning of the second half, with Benfica down 0–4, Béla Guttmann decided to bring Eusébio from the bench to substitute [[Joaquim Santana Silva Guimarães|Santana]]. Shortly after coming in, Santos reached 0–5. However, between the 63rd and the 80th minute, Eusébio scored 3 goals and suffered a foul inside the penalty area, the penalty taker, [[José Augusto de Almeida|José Augusto]], failed to score though. The game finished 6–3 for Santos, with Eusébio being on the cover of the famed French sporting newspaper ''[[L'Équipe]]''.

[[File:Beufica tegen Real Madrid 5-3 spelmoment, Bestanddeelnr 913-8524.jpg|thumb|right|Eusébio strikes against Real Madrid during the [[1962 European Cup Final]].]]
His following season was the one where he started to gain global recognition among football fans and critics alike. He scored 12 goals in 17 league matches, and even though the club finished third, they won the Taça de Portugal against Vitória de Setúbal, with Eusébio scoring two goals in the final. In that same season, he won the [[1961–62 European Cup|European Cup]], also scoring two goals in the [[1962 European Cup Final|final]] against [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] in a 5–3 result to Benfica. Due to his fine form during the season, he finished second in the 1962 [[Ballon d'Or]], in his first complete season as a professional. In October 1963, he was selected to represent the [[FIFA]] team in the "Golden Anniversary" of [[The Football Association]] at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]].

[[File:Beufica tegen Real Madrid 5-3 (blijdschap van de speler, Bestanddeelnr 913-8511.jpg|thumb|left|Eusébio celebrating Benfica's 1962 European Cup victory]]
Benfica were also [[European Cup]] runners-up in [[1962–63 European Cup|1963]], [[1964–65 European Cup|1965]] and [[1967–68 European Cup|1968]]. In the 1968 defeat to the English league champions [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at Wembley Stadium, with the scores 1–1, he came close to winning the game for Benfica in the dying seconds of the game, only to have his shot saved by [[Alex Stepney]]. Despite this, and the fact that the English side went on to win 4–1 in extra time, he openly congratulated Stepney for his efforts throughout the game, stopping to applaud Stepney as he threw the ball back into play.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0254-0d7cbdf21036-42f02a9cf29d-1000--eusebio-to-receive-uefa-president-s-award/ Eusébio to receive UEFA President's Award –] . Uefa.com. Retrieved on 8 May 2011.</ref>

He received a number of individual accolades and awards while playing for Benfica. He was the 1965 European Footballer of the Year (Ballon d'Or) and finished as runner-up twice, in 1962 and 1966, and in 1968 was the first winner of the [[European Golden Boot|Golden Boot]] Award, as Europe's leading scorer, a feat he repeated five years later. He was the [[Portuguese Liga|Portuguese First Division]]'s top scorer seven times (1964, 1965, 1966, 1967, 1968, 1970 and 1973), helping Benfica to win 11 Primeira Liga (1960–61, 1962–63, 1963–64, 1964–65, 1966–67, 1967–68, 1968–69, 1970–71, 1971–72, 1972–73 and 1974–75), 5 Portuguese Cup wins (1961–62, 1963–64, 1968–69, 1969–70 and 1971–72), 1 [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] win (1961–62) and 3 European Cup finals (1962–63, 1964–65 and 1967–68).

Eusébio scored 473 goals in 440 official matches for Benfica,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=451283 |title=Morreu Eusébio |language=pt |trans-title=Eusébio died |date=5 January 2014 |work=[[A Bola]] |access-date=1 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109183228/http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=451283 |archive-date=9 January 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=7 December 2016|title=Leo Messi draws level with Eusebio for number of goals with the same club|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/813743/leo-messi-draws-level-with-eusebio-for-number-of-goals-with-the-same-club|work=FC Barcelona|access-date=25 September 2019|archive-date=25 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925183602/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/813743/leo-messi-draws-level-with-eusebio-for-number-of-goals-with-the-same-club|url-status=live}}</ref> including 317 goals in 301 Primeira Liga matches,<ref name="fifabio">{{cite web |url=http://fifaworldcup.yahoo.com/06/en/p/cp/por/eusebio.html |title=World Cup classic players – Eusebio |date=26 October 2006 |website=fifaworldcup.yahoo.com |publisher=[[FIFA]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051207155708/http://fifaworldcup.yahoo.com/06/en/p/cp/por/eusebio.html |archive-date=7 December 2005 |url-status=dead |access-date=1 February 2015 }}</ref> and 59 goals in 78 matches of [[UEFA]] club competitions. Overall, he scored 727 goals in 715 matches wearing Benfica's jersey.<ref name="totals">{{cite web|url=http://pt.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=por/news/newsid=2041745.html|title=Benfica e Portugal de luto por Eusébio|language=pt|website=[[UEFA]]|date=6 January 2014|access-date=6 January 2014|archive-date=6 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106031456/http://pt.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=por/news/newsid=2041745.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Later career===
[[File:Pele joy eusebio.jpg|thumb|right|Eusébio (right) with [[Pelé]] (left) and [[Brian Joy]] (centre) before a game in the [[North American Soccer League (1968–84)|NASL]] in April 1977]]
In 1976–77 and 1977–78, Eusébio played for two smaller Portuguese clubs, [[S.C. Beira-Mar|Beira-Mar]], in the first division, and [[União de Tomar]], in the [[Portuguese Second Division|Second Division]].

He also played in the [[North American Soccer League (1968–1984)|North American Soccer League]] (NASL), for three different teams, from 1975 to 1977: [[Boston Minutemen]] (1975), [[Toronto Metros-Croatia]] (1976), and the [[Las Vegas Quicksilvers]] (1977).<ref>{{cite news |date=7 February 1977 |title=Sports Shorts: Soccer |page=4B |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21138160/eusbio_traded_to_las_vegas/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=20 June 2018 |archive-date=21 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621042917/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21138160/eusbio_traded_to_las_vegas/ |url-status=live }} {{open access}}</ref> His most successful season in the NASL was in [[1976 North American Soccer League season|1976]] with Toronto Metros-Croatia. He scored the winning goal in their 3–0 victory at the [[Soccer Bowl '76]] to win the NASL title.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1314&dat=19760829&id=BCFOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=nO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5541,5535255|title=The Spokesman-Review - Google News Archive Search|website=news.google.com|access-date=9 October 2015|archive-date=12 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312092237/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1314&dat=19760829&id=BCFOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=nO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5541,5535255|url-status=live}}</ref> The same year, he played ten games for [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] in the Mexican league.

The following season (1977), he signed for the Las Vegas Quicksilvers. By this time, injuries had taken their toll on the Black Panther, and he was constantly receiving medical treatment whilst playing for the Quicksilvers. During the season, he only managed to score two goals.

Although his knees robbed him of his ability to continue in the NASL, Eusébio wanted to continue to play soccer. He found a home in 1978 with the [[New Jersey Americans (soccer)|New Jersey Americans]] of the second-tier [[American Soccer League (1933-1983)|American Soccer League]] (ASL). He went on to play five games for the [[Buffalo Stallions]] during the [[1979–80 Major Indoor Soccer League season|1979–80]] [[MISL I|Major Indoor Soccer League]] season. He retired in 1979 and formed part of the technical committee of the [[Portugal national football team]].<ref>''The Soccer Fact Book'', p. 49</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Eusebio Portugal.JPG|thumb|upright|Eusébio as Portugal's captain against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in 1972.]]
Eusébio was the leading scorer for his country, with 41 goals in 64 matches, until [[Pauleta]] equalled and surpassed his record<ref name=worldcup/> against [[Latvia national football team|Latvia]] on 12 October 2005. Eusébio was also the most capped Portuguese player from 1972, until [[Nené (footballer, born 1949)|Nené]] made his 64th cap against [[Yugoslavia national football team|Yugoslavia]] on 2 June 1984 in a friendly match, breaking Eusébio's record during the [[UEFA Euro 1984]] on 20 June against Romania. He made his debut for the Portugal national team against [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]] on 8 October 1961, a match his country lost 4–2, with the player scoring Portugal's first goal in the match.

===1966 World Cup===

After Portugal qualified for the [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966 World Cup]], they were drawn in [[1966 FIFA World Cup#Group 3|Group 3]], alongside [[Bulgaria national football team|Bulgaria]], [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] and the reigning champions Brazil. After a modest performance against Hungary in the first game, Eusébio scored a goal against Bulgaria. Topping the group with two wins, the team would play against the Brazilians for the final group match. With an injured Pelé, Portugal had no trouble in defeating them with two goals from Eusébio, including a famous volley from a tight angle after a corner kick. The result meant Brazil's early elimination.

In the quarter-final, Portugal played [[Korea DPR national football team|North Korea]], who had defeated and eliminated [[Italy national football team|Italy]] in the group stage. After trailing 0–3 in the 25th minute, Eusébio proceeded to score four consecutive goals, two before half time and two in the first fifteen minutes of the second half. His fourth goal in that match came from a penalty when two North Korean players tackled him after a fast run Eusébio had made from the middle of the Portuguese half to the opposition's penalty area. Portugal came back to win 5–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.worldsoccer.com/columnists/keir-radnedge/eusebio-344295|title=Portugal legend Eusebio remembered|last=Rainbow|first=Jamie|date=6 January 2014|website=[[World Soccer (magazine)|World Soccer]]|access-date=12 June 2016|archive-date=12 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612220425/http://www.worldsoccer.com/columnists/keir-radnedge/eusebio-344295|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the semi-final match Portugal faced [[England national football team|England]]; taking a last-minute train trip from Liverpool to [[London]]. Throughout the game Eusébio was closely marked by England's defensive midfielder [[Nobby Stiles]], but still managed to score Portugal's only goal from the penalty spot in the 82nd minute, ending yet-to-be broken records of seven consecutive [[Shutout|clean sheets]] and 708 minutes without conceding a goal for the English team.<ref name="on this day">{{cite web |url=http://www.givemefootball.com/premier-league/on-this-day-in-football-history-july-26 |title=Not even the great Eusebio can halt England's World Cup march |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100731054546/http://www.givemefootball.com/premier-league/on-this-day-in-football-history-july-26 |archive-date=31 July 2010 |access-date=8 February 2011 |first=John |last=Harding |date=26 July 2010 |work=Give me Football}}</ref> After scoring the penalty, Eusébio went on to catch the ball and saluted [[Gordon Banks]]. The goal was not enough to nullify [[Bobby Charlton]]'s two earlier goals. [[António Simões]] had a last-minute chance only for Stiles to make it into a corner. Portugal lost 1–2 and Eusébio famously walked off the pitch in tears, being comforted by both his teammates and opponents. The game is known as the ''Jogo das Lágrimas'' (Game of Tears) in Portugal.

In the third place match, Portugal played against the [[Soviet Union national football team|Soviet Union]]. In the 12th minute after a handball inside the area, Eusébio scored the opening goal (his ninth and final World Cup goal) from the penalty spot. Although [[Lev Yashin]] guessed the side in which the ball would go, he was powerless to save it. Again and as he had done before with Banks, Eusébio went to salute his friend Yashin after he had scored. Portugal won the game 2–1 in what remains their best ever World Cup participation, and the best performance by a team on its debut since Italy's victory in [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]].

In addition to winning the [[World Cup Golden Boot|Golden Boot]] (with nine goals) for the 1966 World Cup, Eusébio also set a record that year for the most penalties scored (shoot-out not included), with four. Eusébio's four goals against North Korea in the quarter-final match also helped Portugal tie the record for largest deficit overcome in a win (three goals, equaling [[Austria national football team|Austria]] in [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]) and he became the fifth player to score as many goals in a [[FIFA World Cup]] match, a record he jointly held until [[Oleg Salenko]] scored five in the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994 World Cup]]. The English were so impressed by Eusébio's performances that his waxwork was immediately added to the [[Madame Tussauds]] in London.<ref name="on this day"/> He also received the [[BBC Overseas Sports Personality of the Year]] for 1966.<ref name="Sports personality"/>

==Personal life==
[[File:Aankomst Benfica op Schiphol, Eusebio, Bestanddeelnr 925-5028.jpg|thumb|Eusébio accompanied by his wife, Flora, in April 1972]]
Eusébio was a devout [[Roman Catholic]] and married Flora Claudina Bruheim on 8 October 1965.<ref>[http://largodoscorreios.wordpress.com/category/pessoas/eusebio-da-silva-ferreira/ Eusébio da Silva Ferreira] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812033733/http://largodoscorreios.wordpress.com/category/pessoas/eusebio-da-silva-ferreira/ |date=12 August 2014 }}. largodoscorreios.wordpress.com</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Casamento de Eusébio e Flora |url=https://arquivos.rtp.pt/conteudos/casamento-de-eusebio-e-flora/ |access-date=9 October 2023 |language=pt |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030220733/https://arquivos.rtp.pt/conteudos/casamento-de-eusebio-e-flora/ |url-status=live }}</ref> They had two daughters together, Carla Elisa Bruheim da Silva Ferreira (born 1968) and Sandra Judite Bruheim da Silva Ferreira (born 1969).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://caras.sapo.pt/famosos/2014/01/26/especial-eusebio---familia/|title=Especial Eusébio - Família, Revista Caras, 26-01-2014}}</ref>

Eusébio said he went to the [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|Portuguese Parliament]] eight times to talk to [[António de Oliveira Salazar]] who ruled the country from 1932 to 1968 as the virtual dictator of the [[Estado Novo (Portugal)|Estado Novo]] regime. Eusébio had invitations from big clubs in Europe, and was interested in signing for them, but could not because the "godfather", as he recalled Salazar, would not let him go.<ref name=":0" />

After the [[Carnation Revolution]] of 1974 in Lisbon and the subsequent independence of Portugal's overseas territory of Mozambique as the [[People's Republic of Mozambique]] in 1975, Eusébio lost all of his property and investments in the African country.<ref name=":0" />

In a 2011 interview, Eusébio said that he did not like Sporting Lourenço Marques (Sporting CP's affiliate club in Mozambique) because in his neighbourhood<ref name=":62" /> it was deemed a club of the elites and the police, which did not like [[people of color]]. Eusébio described the club as "[[racist]]".<ref name=":0" /> Moreover, he also said he did not like Sporting CP while mentioning the kidnapping story "they made up" regarding his transfer to Benfica: "What I do not like is Sporting [CP]" [...] "I do not even like Sporting from there [Mozambique], let alone the one from here [Portugal]".<ref name="tribuna.expresso.pt"/> Eusébio liked Desportivo Lourenço Marques, Benfica's feeder team in Mozambique that shared identical symbols and motto with Benfica,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=EUSÉBIO NO SPORTING? por Rui Alves - Replay, RTP Memoria - Canais TV - RTP |url=https://www.rtp.pt/rtpmemoria/replay/eusebio-no-sportingt-por-rui-alves_421 |access-date=2024-04-07 |website=www.rtp.pt |language=pt}}</ref> just like his brother and late father.<ref name=":0" />

After he had been accepted by Sporting Lourenço Marques together with a group of friends from his neighbourhood,<ref name=":62" /> in the course of an interview a day after Eusébio's first match for Sporting Lourenço Marques in which he scored three goals, Eusébio accused Desportivo Lourenço Marques head coach of being a racist, and, according to Eusébio, Desportivo's head coach was fired shortly after.<ref name=":0" />

==Death==
Eusébio died at his home on 5 January 2014 of [[heart failure]], aged 71.<ref>Hatton, Barry (5 January 2014) [https://web.archive.org/web/20140106031744/http://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/report-eusebio-dead-71-heart-failure-21425081 Eusebio, Portugal's Beloved Soccer Giant, Dies]. Associated Press via ABC News</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/05/eusebio-portugal-football-hero-dies-71|title= Eusébio, Portugal's footballing hero, dies at 71|date=5 January 2014|work=Guardian|access-date=8 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140105103423/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/05/eusebio-portugal-football-hero-dies-71|archive-date=5 January 2014}}</ref> Many well-known people from the football world expressed their condolences and praise, including his contemporaries [[Franz Beckenbauer]] and [[Bobby Charlton]].<ref name="Tributes">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25612337 |title=Eusebio: Football figures pay tribute to Portugal legend |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 January 2014 |access-date=6 January 2014 |archive-date=6 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106104141/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/25612337 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Portuguese Football Federation made a statement and said that a moment of silence was to be observed in Portuguese football matches. There were tributes from [[Cristiano Ronaldo]],<ref name="Tributes"/> [[Luís Figo]],<ref>{{cite news |last=Orr |first=James |title=Eusebio: Death of 'immortal' Portuguese football great sparks tributes from Cristiano Ronaldo and Jose Mourinho |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/eusebio-death-of-immortal-portuguese-football-great-sparks-tributes-from-cristiano-ronaldo-and-jose-9039824.html |date=5 January 2014 |access-date=22 June 2018 |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |archive-date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622034001/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/eusebio-death-of-immortal-portuguese-football-great-sparks-tributes-from-cristiano-ronaldo-and-jose-9039824.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[José Mourinho]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/soccer/portugal-mourns-eusebio-1628681|title=Portugal mourns Eusebio|website=www.iol.co.za|access-date=14 February 2021|archive-date=21 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421075147/https://www.iol.co.za/sport/soccer/portugal-mourns-eusebio-1628681|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Carlos Queiroz]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.persianfootball.com/news/2014/01/06/the-legendary-eusebio-scored-goal-against-iran/,%20http://www.persianfootball.com/news/2014/01/06/the-legendary-eusebio-scored-goal-against-iran/|title=The legendary Eusebio scored a goal against Iran}}</ref><ref>[http://www.goal.com/iran/news/1825/%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86/2014/01/06/4524165/ناراحتی شدید کی روش از درگذشت اوزه بیو/ او حد و مرز نداشت Carlos Queiroz's interview with Tehran-e Emrooz]. goal.com. 6 January 2014</ref> FIFA President [[Sepp Blatter]]<ref name="Tributes"/> UEFA president [[Michel Platini]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140106034323/http://www.uefa.org/aboutuefa/organisation/president/news/newsid%3D2041746.html Michel Platini pays tribute to 'true legend' Eusébio]. uefa.org. 5 January 2014</ref> [[Greg Dyke]], and former President of Mozambique and childhood friend [[Joaquim Chissano]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=451297 |title="Perdi um amigo, Eusébio era um orgulho para o povo moçambicano" – Joaquim Chissano |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106034408/http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=451297 |archive-date=6 January 2014 |work=A Bola |language=pt}}</ref> 
[[File:Lisbon, Pantheon, tomb of Eusébio.JPG|thumb|right|Eusébio's tomb in the [[Church of Santa Engrácia|National Pantheon]], Lisbon]]
Following Eusébio's death, the [[government of Portugal|Portuguese government]] declared three days of national mourning. Hundreds of thousands paid tribute to him.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://en.wikinews.org/wiki/Portuguese_government_declares_three_days_of_mourning_for_Eus%C3%A9bio|title=Portuguese government declares three days of mourning for Eusébio – Wikinews, the free news source|date=5 January 2014|newspaper=[[Wikinews]]|access-date=6 January 2014|archive-date=6 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106040515/http://en.wikinews.org/wiki/Portuguese_government_declares_three_days_of_mourning_for_Eus%C3%A9bio|url-status=live}}</ref> On 6 January 2014, a mass was held at the Igreja do Seminário do Largo da Luz. On 9 January, one of his wishes was granted as his coffin was transported around the field of the [[Estádio da Luz]].<ref name="totals"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jn.pt/PaginaInicial/Desporto/Interior.aspx?content_id=3615434|title=Eusébio homenageado no Estádio da Luz|language=pt|website=Jornal de Noticias|date=6 January 2014|access-date=6 January 2014|archive-date=6 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106032141/http://www.jn.pt/PaginaInicial/Desporto/Interior.aspx?content_id=3615434|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-25621432|title=Eusebio funeral: Thousands line streets to say farewell|date=6 January 2014|work=BBC News|access-date=8 January 2014|archive-date=7 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140107165411/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-25621432|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, his statue (inaugurated on his 50th birthday)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arquivos.rtp.pt/conteudos/homenagem-a-eusebio/|title=Homenagem a Eusébio|last=Sousa|first=Helena Sousa e|date=25 January 1992|website=RTP Arquivos|language=pt|trans-title=Homage to Eusébio|access-date=4 May 2018|archive-date=4 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504231238/https://arquivos.rtp.pt/conteudos/homenagem-a-eusebio/|url-status=live}}</ref> at the ''Praça Centenarium'' was transformed into a memorial.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/33814/language/pt-PT/Estrutura-da-estatua-do-Eusebio-esta-a-ser-erguida.aspx |title=Estrutura da estátua do Eusébio está a ser erguida |trans-title=Structure of Eusébio statue is being built |date=9 January 2014 |publisher=S.L. Benfica |access-date=9 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110090842/http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/33814/language/pt-PT/Estrutura-da-estatua-do-Eusebio-esta-a-ser-erguida.aspx |archive-date=10 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/33848/language/pt-PT/Estrutura-da-estatua-do-Pantera-Negra-esta-terminada.aspx |title=Estrutura da estátua do "Pantera Negra" está terminada |trans-title=Structure of the "Black Panther" statue is concluded |date=12 January 2014 |publisher=S.L. Benfica |access-date=12 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112135054/http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/33848/language/pt-PT/Estrutura-da-estatua-do-Pantera-Negra-esta-terminada.aspx |archive-date=12 January 2014}}</ref> Hours later, the name "Eusébio" was on the back of every Benfica players' shirts during "[[O Clássico]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25684413 |title=BBC Sport – Benfica 2–0 FC Porto |date=12 January 2014 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=13 January 2014 |archive-date=12 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112221801/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/25684413 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Precisely one year after his death, the avenue in front of the Estádio da Luz was renamed ''Avenida Eusébio da Silva Ferreira'', becoming its new address.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/40030/language/pt-PT/Morada-do-Estadio-da-Luz-muda-para-Eusebio-da-Silva-Ferreira.aspx |title=Morada do Estádio da Luz muda para Eusébio da Silva Ferreira |language=pt |trans-title=Estádio da Luz address changes to Eusébio da Silva Ferreira |date=5 January 2015 |website=[[S.L. Benfica]] |access-date=5 January 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107183134/http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/40030/language/pt-PT/Morada-do-Estadio-da-Luz-muda-para-Eusebio-da-Silva-Ferreira.aspx |archive-date=7 January 2015}}</ref> On 3 July, his remains were moved to the [[Church of Santa Engrácia|National Pantheon]], where notable Portuguese personalities are buried. Parliament voted unanimously for him to be interred there. Eusébio was the first footballer to be buried at the Pantheon.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.supersport.com/football/portugal/news/150703/Portugal_makes_final_tribute_to_Eusebio |title=Portugal makes final tribute to Eusebio |date=3 July 2015 |publisher=SuperSport |access-date=4 July 2015 |archive-date=5 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705034552/http://www.supersport.com/football/portugal/news/150703/Portugal_makes_final_tribute_to_Eusebio |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2019, Eusébio was, along with [[Maria Mutola]], referred by [[Pope Francis]] as an example of perseverance, during the latter's visit to Mozambique.<ref>{{cite news|date=9 September 2019|title=Pope offers Mozambican youth two models of perseverance: Eusébio and Mutola, who never gave up fighting for their dreams|url=https://clubofmozambique.com/news/pope-offers-mozambican-youth-two-models-of-perseverance-eusebio-and-mutola-who-never-gave-up-fighting-for-their-dreams-watch-141320/|work=Club of Mozambique|access-date=9 September 2019|archive-date=9 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909175630/https://clubofmozambique.com/news/pope-offers-mozambican-youth-two-models-of-perseverance-eusebio-and-mutola-who-never-gave-up-fighting-for-their-dreams-watch-141320/|url-status=live}}</ref> Eusébio has been called "Africa's first great footballer"<ref name="worldcup" /> and "Africa's greatest-ever player".<ref name="worldcup" />
